topLevel.title: The Civil Engineer's Guide to AI

subs.title: 1.1 What is Artificial Intelligence?
subs.description: Explore the foundations of Artificial Intelligence through the lens of civil engineering. Learn what AI is, how it works, and why it matters for modern infrastructure.

subs.title: 1.2 AI Capabilities — Perception, Reasoning, Learning, Interaction
subs.description: Explore AI's four core capabilities - Perception, Reasoning, Learning, and Interaction - through civil engineering analogies, interactive demos, and real-world applications.

subs.title: 1.3 AI Subfields — Computer Vision, NLP, Robotics & More
subs.description: Explore the major subfields of Artificial Intelligence - Computer Vision, NLP, Robotics, Expert Systems, Planning, Speech Recognition, and ML - with civil engineering applications, interactive demos, and quizzes.

subs.title: 1.4 What is Machine Learning? — Core Concepts
subs.description: Understand Machine Learning from the ground up: the shift from programming rules to learning from data. Interactive demos, civil engineering analogies, and quizzes for engineers.

subs.title: 1.5 The ML Pipeline — Data to Deployment
subs.description: Walk through the complete Machine Learning pipeline from problem definition to deployment. Interactive demos, civil engineering analogies, and quizzes for engineers.

subs.title: 1.6 AI vs ML — The Critical Distinction
subs.description: Understand the crucial difference between Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. Interactive Venn diagrams, classification games, and decision guides for civil engineers.

subs.title: 1.7 The Dam vs River Analogy — Central Metaphor
subs.description: The central metaphor: AI is the Dam (engineered system), ML is the River (data flow). Interactive dam simulation, component explorer, and deep analogy mapping for civil engineers.

subs.title: 1.8 Types of Machine Learning — Supervised, Unsupervised, RL, Semi-supervised
subs.description: Explore the four main types of machine learning — supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, and semi-supervised learning — with civil engineering analogies, interactive demos, and quizzes.

subs.title: 1.9 Introduction to Deep Learning — Neural Networks
subs.description: Explore the fundamentals of deep learning and neural networks through a civil engineering lens. Learn about neurons, layers, backpropagation, and why depth matters — with interactive demos and quizzes.

subs.title: 1.10 Bias, Ethics & CE Applications
subs.description: Explore bias in AI/ML systems, ethical considerations for civil engineering, and a comprehensive overview of real-world AI applications in structural health monitoring, crack detection, traffic optimization, and more.

subs.title: 2.1 Supervised Learning Fundamentals
subs.description: Master the fundamentals of supervised learning through a civil engineering lens. Understand features, labels, training workflows, regression vs classification, and real-world CE applications.

subs.title: 2.2 Linear Regression
subs.description: Master linear regression from a civil engineering perspective. Learn the equation y = mx + b, least squares, gradient descent, cost functions, R-squared, and predict concrete strength from water-cement ratio.

subs.title: 2.3 Polynomial & Multiple Regression
subs.description: Go beyond straight lines with polynomial regression and multiple linear regression. Learn to model nonlinear soil stress-strain curves, predict concrete strength from multiple mix factors, understand multicollinearity, and master adjusted R-squared.

subs.title: 2.4 Classification Basics
subs.description: Learn the fundamentals of classification in machine learning through a civil engineering lens. Understand binary and multi-class classification, decision boundaries, k-nearest neighbours, confusion matrices, and real-world applications such as pass/fail testing, soil classification, and safety compliance.

subs.title: 2.5 Logistic Regression
subs.description: Master logistic regression for civil engineering applications. Understand the sigmoid function, log-odds, probability thresholds, binary cross-entropy loss, multi-class softmax, and real-world CE applications such as failure prediction and dam safety classification.

subs.title: 2.6 Decision Trees & Random Forests
subs.description: Master decision trees and random forests for civil engineering. Understand splitting criteria (Gini impurity, information gain), tree construction, pruning, overfitting, bagging, feature randomness, and ensemble voting with applications to material selection and structural risk assessment.

subs.title: 2.7 Support Vector Machines
subs.description: Master Support Vector Machines for civil engineering applications. Understand maximum margin hyperplanes, support vectors, soft margin (C parameter), the kernel trick (linear, polynomial, RBF), SVR, and applications to earthquake damage classification and soil liquefaction prediction.

subs.title: 2.8 Model Evaluation Metrics
subs.description: Master model evaluation metrics for civil engineering AI applications. Learn classification metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, confusion matrix), regression metrics (MAE, MSE, RMSE, R-squared), and cross-validation techniques with interactive demos.

subs.title: 2.9 Overfitting, Underfitting & Regularization
subs.description: Understand overfitting, underfitting, the bias-variance tradeoff, and regularization techniques (L1, L2, Elastic Net, dropout, early stopping) with interactive demos and civil engineering analogies.

subs.title: 2.10 CE Case Study: Site Response Analysis
subs.description: End-to-end supervised learning case study predicting seismic site response (ground motion amplification) from soil properties using ML. Capstone sub-chapter for Chapter 2.

subs.title: 3.1 Unsupervised Learning Fundamentals
subs.description: Explore unsupervised learning fundamentals through a civil engineering lens. Understand clustering, dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection, and how machines discover hidden patterns without labelled data.

subs.title: 3.2 K-Means Clustering
subs.description: Master K-Means clustering through a civil engineering lens. Learn the algorithm step by step, choose the right K with elbow and silhouette methods, cluster soil samples and traffic data, and explore interactive demos.

subs.title: 3.3 Hierarchical Clustering
subs.description: Learn hierarchical clustering for civil engineering applications. Explore agglomerative and divisive approaches, linkage methods, dendrograms, and interactive demos for material classification and bridge condition grouping.

subs.title: 3.4 DBSCAN & Density-Based Methods
subs.description: Learn DBSCAN and density-based clustering for civil engineering. Explore epsilon neighborhoods, core/border/noise classification, geospatial sensor clusters, damage zone detection, and interactive demos comparing DBSCAN with K-Means.

subs.title: 3.5 Dimensionality Reduction — PCA
subs.description: Learn Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for civil engineering. Explore the curse of dimensionality, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, explained variance, scree plots, and interactive demos for reducing multi-sensor bridge monitoring data and compressing soil test results.

subs.title: 3.6 t-SNE & UMAP Visualization
subs.description: Learn t-SNE and UMAP for non-linear dimensionality reduction and visualization. Explore perplexity, probability distributions, fuzzy topological sets, and interactive demos comparing PCA versus t-SNE on multi-sensor SHM data for civil engineering.

subs.title: 3.7 Anomaly Detection
subs.description: Learn statistical and machine-learning anomaly detection methods including z-score, IQR, Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor, and autoencoders. Explore interactive demos for detecting sensor malfunctions, unusual settlement, and structural response anomalies in civil engineering.

subs.title: 3.8 Association Rules & Pattern Mining
subs.description: Learn association rule mining with Apriori and FP-growth algorithms. Explore support, confidence, and lift metrics applied to construction defect co-occurrence, material procurement patterns, and safety incident correlations.

subs.title: 3.9 Evaluating Unsupervised Models
subs.description: Learn how to evaluate unsupervised learning models using silhouette scores, the elbow method, Davies-Bouldin index, and Calinski-Harabasz index. Explore visual inspection strategies and civil engineering applications for validating soil clustering and damage pattern grouping.

subs.title: 3.10 CE Case Study: GIS Land Classification
subs.description: End-to-end unsupervised learning case study: classifying land use from satellite imagery using spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI) and K-Means clustering for urban planning, environmental assessment, and site selection.

subs.title: 4.1 Images as Data
subs.description: Understand how computers see images as numerical data. Explore pixels, grayscale vs color, RGB channels, resolution, and image tensors through a civil engineering lens with interactive demos.

subs.title: 4.2 Convolution Operation
subs.description: Learn the convolution operation: sliding kernels over images, element-wise multiplication and summation, padding, stride, and common filters like Sobel edge detection. Interactive demos with civil engineering examples.

subs.title: 4.3 Pooling & Stride
subs.description: Understand pooling layers (max, average, global average) and stride as a downsampling alternative. Interactive demos with civil engineering examples: reducing drone image features while preserving crack information.

subs.title: 4.4 CNN Architecture
subs.description: Build a complete CNN architecture: stacking convolutional layers, pooling, flatten, fully connected layers, ReLU, softmax, batch normalization, dropout, receptive fields, and feature hierarchy. Interactive CNN builder and feature hierarchy visualizer for crack classification.

subs.title: 4.5 Training CNNs
subs.description: How to train Convolutional Neural Networks: forward pass, loss computation, backpropagation, weight update, data augmentation for civil engineering imagery, transfer learning for crack detection, learning rate scheduling, and batch size effects. Interactive data augmentation gallery and training progress monitor.

subs.title: 4.6 Famous CNN Architectures
subs.description: A tour of landmark CNN architectures from LeNet-5 (1998) to EfficientNet: AlexNet, VGG, GoogLeNet/Inception, ResNet, DenseNet, and MobileNet. Key innovations, civil engineering relevance, interactive architecture timeline, and residual connection visualizer.

subs.title: 4.7 Object Detection
subs.description: From image classification to object detection: anchor boxes, IoU, Non-Maximum Suppression, mAP, two-stage vs one-stage detectors (R-CNN family, YOLO, SSD). Interactive IoU calculator and NMS visualizer. Civil engineering applications for crack detection, spalling, rebar exposure, and safety equipment monitoring.

subs.title: 4.8 Semantic Segmentation
subs.description: Pixel-level classification with encoder-decoder architectures, FCN, U-Net skip connections, transposed convolution, dice loss, and IoU per class. Civil engineering applications for crack segmentation, damage mapping, and road surface analysis. Interactive segmentation painter and U-Net architecture diagram.

subs.title: 4.9 Visualizing CNN Internals
subs.description: Explore CNN interpretability techniques including feature map visualization, filter visualization, Grad-CAM, saliency maps, occlusion sensitivity, and t-SNE for civil engineering applications. Understand what a crack detector sees and build trust in AI for structural assessment.

subs.title: 4.10 CE Case Study: Crack Detection
subs.description: End-to-end case study building a CNN-based crack detection system for concrete infrastructure. Covers dataset preparation, ResNet-18 transfer learning, training, evaluation with confusion matrix and ROC curves, Grad-CAM validation, and edge deployment on inspection drones.

subs.title: 5.1 Sequence Models & RNNs
subs.description: Understand sequence models and recurrent neural networks through a civil engineering lens. Explore RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, and bidirectional architectures for sensor time series and specification text processing.

subs.title: 5.2 The Attention Mechanism
subs.description: Understand the attention mechanism through a civil engineering lens. Explore Query, Key, Value vectors, scaled dot-product attention, and self-attention with interactive demos and analogies.

subs.title: 5.3 Transformer Architecture
subs.description: Master the Transformer architecture through a civil engineering lens. Explore multi-head attention, positional encoding, encoder-decoder stacks, residual connections, and layer normalization with interactive demos.

subs.title: 5.4 BERT & Encoder Models
subs.description: Explore BERT and encoder-only Transformer models through a civil engineering lens. Learn masked language modelling, next sentence prediction, fine-tuning, tokenization, and variants like RoBERTa, ALBERT, and DistilBERT with interactive demos.

subs.title: 5.5 GPT & Decoder Models
subs.description: Explore GPT and decoder-only Transformer models through a civil engineering lens. Learn autoregressive generation, causal masking, temperature sampling, top-k/top-p, GPT evolution from GPT-1 to GPT-4, in-context learning, and few-shot prompting with interactive demos.

subs.title: 5.6 Tokenization & Embeddings
subs.description: Learn how text is broken into tokens and mapped to numerical vectors. Explore BPE, WordPiece, SentencePiece, Word2Vec, GloVe, contextual embeddings, positional encodings, and context windows with interactive demos and civil engineering analogies.

subs.title: 5.7 Fine-Tuning & Prompt Engineering
subs.description: Master the two main strategies for adapting large language models to civil engineering tasks: fine-tuning model weights on domain data and crafting effective prompts. Covers LoRA, QLoRA, adapters, RLHF, zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought prompting, and CE-specific applications.

subs.title: 5.8 RAG & Knowledge Retrieval
subs.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for civil engineering: ground LLM outputs in building codes, project specifications, and safety manuals using embedding-based retrieval, vector databases, chunking strategies, and hybrid search.

subs.title: 5.9 LLM Limitations & Hallucinations
subs.description: Understand the failure modes of large language models: hallucination, confabulation, sycophancy, reasoning errors, bias amplification, adversarial attacks, and civil-engineering-specific risks including fabricated code references and incorrect load calculations.

subs.title: 5.10 CE Case Study: AI-Assisted Design Review
subs.description: End-to-end case study of using NLP and LLMs for AI-assisted structural design review in civil engineering: document ingestion, information extraction, code compliance checking, automated report generation, and human sign-off.

subs.title: 6.1 The Perceptron - From Biology to Math | CE Guide to AI
6.2 Multi-Layer Networks & Forward Propagation
subs.description: From a single perceptron to a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP). Learn forward propagation, matrix notation, and why depth matters - explained for civil engineers.

subs.title: 6.3 Activation Functions | A Civil Engineer's Guide to AI
6.4 Loss Functions
subs.description: Understand loss functions: MSE, MAE, Huber, cross-entropy and how they shape neural network learning, with civil engineering analogies.

subs.title: 6.10 CE Case Study: Concrete Strength Prediction
